small_guidance:
- Add larger GEMM tiles to the autotune list (e.g. `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32/64` with `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=3`) — current best is likely 64×64 or 64×128 which under-utilizes a 4090's tensor cores for OC=64, NOUT=62·62·14 ≈ 53816.
- Since OC=64 is tiny, fix `BLOCK_M=64` (one tile covers all OC) and push `BLOCK_N` to 128/256 and `BLOCK_K` to 64/128 so K (=216) is covered in 2-4 iterations; this reduces redundant weight reloads across the spatial tile.
- Preload the entire weight matrix (OC×K = 64×216 = ~54KB fp32) once into shared memory / registers outside the K loop (or process all K in a single unrolled pass with `BLOCK_K=K_TOTAL` rounded up to 256) — eliminates repeated weight gathers.
large_guidance:
- Switch input layout to channels-last (NDHWC) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC·kT·kH·kW) is contiguous on the inner stride; the current NCDHW gather makes `x_tile` loads strided by D·H·W across IC, killing coalescing on the K axis. Pre-permute `x` once in `forward` and permute output back (or write output channels-last and permute on store).
- Restructure parallelism: with OC=64 small, use one program per `(batch, output-spatial tile)` covering full OC in registers; accumulate into `(OC, BLOCK_N)` with `BLOCK_N=128-256`. Use grid `(N, cdiv(NOUT, BLOCK_N))` and a single K-loop that streams `(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N)` input tiles — this is the standard implicit-GEMM-for-small-OC shape and avoids 3D grid overhead.
- Specialize the kernel for `KT=KH=KW=3` (compile-time unroll the 27-tap inner loop instead of an im2col K-loop), and load each input channel slice once per spatial tile reusing it across all 27 kernel offsets — dramatically reduces global-memory traffic vs. the current generic implicit GEMM.
